name: Half Berkshire, half famous investors' momentum picks
rules: Half the money: Berkshire Hathaway's top 5 stocks at Berkshire's own weights, from its newest 13F.

Half the money: take the 3 biggest holdings of each of 23 well-known investors (their newest 13F, if filed in the last 200 days), and hold the 5 whose price rose most from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, 10% each.
Rebuilt on the first trading day of every month. The account then rebalances to the new targets at the next open.
caveats: The settings (each investor's top 3, hold 5, 12-month move) were picked after looking at these same years, so the result is flattering. Picking them fresh each year from the 4 years before gave 21.7% a year for the momentum half alone, with a worst drop of 40%.
It is fragile: holding the top 8 momentum picks instead of 5 cut the result to about 17% a year, roughly the old strategy.
2024 (+66%) carries much of the gain. In 3 of 6 years it did worse than the old Berkshire-only plan.
About 11 to 17% of the investors' top holdings had no price history, often companies that were bought out or went bust. Leaving them out flatters a strategy that buys recent winners.
GameStop's January 2021 jump (+1,200%) is left out of these numbers; with it the test looks far better, which is luck, not skill.
Trading cost of 0.1% of every dollar traded is included. Taxes are not. Monthly rebalancing would create many short-term gains in a real taxable account.
